NimbusSec operates a layered security assurance program combining continuous automated testing with periodic independent assessment.

Static and dynamic analysis. All code changes pass static application security testing (SAST) and dependency scanning in CI before merge. Dynamic scans (DAST) run nightly against a staging environment that mirrors production.

Vulnerability management. Infrastructure and container images are scanned weekly. Findings are triaged by severity with remediation SLAs of 7 days (critical), 30 days (high), and 90 days (medium).

Bug bounty. We operate a private bug bounty program through HackerOne with approximately 200 invited researchers. Rewards range from $250 to $20,000 depending on severity.

Red team exercises. An internal red team conducts adversary simulation exercises twice a year, with findings briefed to the executive team.

Independent penetration testing. A CREST-certified third party performs a full-scope penetration test of the platform and supporting infrastructure

twice per year, most recently in August 2025. Testing covers the web application, public APIs, authentication flows, and cloud configuration. Customers may review the executive summary of the most recent report under NDA through our trust portal, and enterprise customers may request the full technical report. Retesting of critical and high findings is performed within 30 days and confirmed closed before the report is finalised.

Customer-initiated testing. Customers may conduct their own penetration testing of the platform against a dedicated test tenancy with 10 business days' notice under our testing agreement.

Compliance verification. Control effectiveness is independently examined annually as part of our SOC 2 Type II audit.

Metrics and reporting. Assurance metrics, including time-to-remediate and test coverage, are reported monthly to the CISO and quarterly to the board risk committee.

Before engaging any third party that will access company or customer information, NimbusSec performs a risk assessment proportionate to the data involved. Assessment includes review of independent audit reports (SOC 2 or ISO 27001), security questionnaires, financial viability checks, and contractual security schedules including breach notification obligations. Vendors handling Confidential or Restricted data are reassessed annually and monitored continuously through a third-party risk platform that alerts on breaches, certificate expiry, and adverse findings. High-risk findings block onboarding until remediated. The vendor register, including risk tier and last assessment date, is reviewed quarterly by the security team.

All customer data stored by the platform is encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM. Storage-level encryption is applied across our primary databases, object storage, search indexes, and backups. Encryption keys are managed in AWS KMS with automatic annual key rotation, and key usage is logged to an immutable audit trail. Customer data in our multi-tenant databases is additionally protected by envelope encryption with per-tenant data keys, so that no single key compromise exposes more than one tenant's records. Field-level encryption is applied to particularly sensitive attributes such as API credentials supplied by customers.

AcmeSat mitigates radio frequency interference (RFI) through a combination of monitoring, coordination, and adaptive operations. Our ground stations run continuous spectrum monitoring with automated anomaly detection that flags interference signatures against known baselines. We coordinate frequency use through the ITU filing process and participate in the Space Data Association for operator-to-operator interference resolution. Operationally, our modems support adaptive coding and modulation, and uplink power control adjusts automatically to maintain link margin during interference events. Persistent interference triggers geolocation analysis to identify the source, with escalation to ACMA or the relevant national regulator where required.

Background verification, including police checks and reference checks, is completed prior to the start date for all roles with access to customer data.

Following contract termination, customer data is retained for 30 days to allow for export, after which it is permanently deleted from production systems. Deletion is completed across all replicas within 7 days of the deletion job commencing, and backup snapshots containing the data expire on a rolling 35-day cycle, meaning all customer data is irrecoverable within a maximum of 72 days of contract end. Secure destruction follows NIST 800-88 guidelines. A certificate of destruction is available on request. Audit logs referencing customer identifiers are retained for 12 months for security purposes, then purged.

Post-incident reviews are completed within 10 business days and shared with affected customers on request.

NimbusSec's use of artificial intelligence is governed by an AI policy approved by the executive team and aligned to the Australian Government's AI Ethics Principles and ISO/IEC 42001 concepts. Key controls include: a register of all AI features and the models behind them; human-in-the-loop review for all AI-generated content before it is sent to end recipients; documented model evaluation before any model change ships to production, covering accuracy, safety, and bias; and vendor assessment of all third-party model providers. An internal AI review board comprising engineering, legal, and security leadership meets monthly to approve new AI use cases and review incidents. Customers can disable AI-assisted features at the workspace level.

All customer data stored by the platform is encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM. Storage-level encryption is applied across our primary databases, object storage, search indexes, and backups. Encryption keys are managed in AWS KMS with automatic annual key rotation, and key usage is logged to an immutable audit trail. Customer data in our multi-tenant databases is additionally protected by envelope encryption with per-tenant data keys, so that no single key compromise exposes more than one tenant's records. Field-level encryption is applied to particularly sensitive attributes such as API credentials supplied by customers.

This document summarises the NimbusSec Information Security Policy suite for customer due-diligence purposes. The policy suite is approved annually by the executive team and applies to all personnel, contractors, and systems.

Governance. Security is overseen by the Chief Information Security Officer, who reports to the CEO and provides quarterly updates to the board risk committee. Policies are reviewed at least annually or after material changes to the business or threat environment.

Risk management. We operate a formal risk register aligned to ISO 27005. Risks are assessed for likelihood and impact, assigned owners, and reviewed quarterly. Residual risks above appetite require executive sign-off.

Asset management. All information assets are inventoried and classified into four tiers: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Handling requirements including encryption,

sharing, and disposal are defined per tier.

Human resources security. Personnel undergo background screening before engagement. Security awareness training is completed at induction and annually thereafter, with phishing simulations run monthly.

Privileged and administrative accounts require a minimum 20-character machine-generated secret stored in the corporate vault,

hardware security key (FIDO2) as the second factor, and rotation every 90 days or immediately upon role change or suspected compromise. Shared credentials are prohibited; break-glass credentials are sealed, monitored, and rotated after each use.

Operations security. Production changes follow a peer-reviewed change management process. Anti-malware and EDR agents are deployed to all endpoints. Vulnerability scanning runs weekly with remediation SLAs of 7 days for critical findings.

Supplier relationships. Suppliers with access to Confidential or Restricted data undergo security assessment before engagement and annually thereafter.

Incident management. Security events are triaged 24/7. Customers are notified of confirmed incidents affecting their data without undue delay and within 72 hours at the latest.

This document summarises the NimbusSec Information Security Policy suite for customer due-diligence purposes. The policy suite is approved annually by the executive team and applies to all personnel, contractors, and systems.

Governance. Security is overseen by the Chief Information Security Officer, who reports to the CEO and provides quarterly updates to the board risk committee. Policies are reviewed at least annually or after material changes to the business or threat environment.

Risk management. We operate a formal risk register aligned to ISO 27005. Risks are assessed for likelihood and impact, assigned owners, and reviewed quarterly. Residual risks above appetite require executive sign-off.

Asset management. All information assets are inventoried and classified into four tiers: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Handling requirements including encryption,

sharing, and disposal are defined per tier.

Human resources security. Personnel undergo background screening before engagement. Security awareness training is completed at induction and annually thereafter, with phishing simulations run monthly.

Access control. Access follows least privilege and is provisioned through role-based profiles. All access to production requires single sign-on with phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication. Privileged access is granted just-in-time and expires after a maximum of 8 hours.

Password and credential requirements. Standard accounts require a minimum 14-character passphrase checked against known-breached password lists, with no forced periodic rotation in line with NIST 800-63B. Privileged and administrative accounts require a minimum 20-character machine-generated secret stored in the corporate vault,

hardware security key (FIDO2) as the second factor, and rotation every 90 days or immediately upon role change or suspected compromise. Shared credentials are prohibited; break-glass credentials are sealed, monitored, and rotated after each use.

Operations security. Production changes follow a peer-reviewed change management process. Anti-malware and EDR agents are deployed to all endpoints. Vulnerability scanning runs weekly with remediation SLAs of 7 days for critical findings.

Supplier relationships. Suppliers with access to Confidential or Restricted data undergo security assessment before engagement and annually thereafter.

Incident management. Security events are triaged 24/7. Customers are notified of confirmed incidents affecting their data without undue delay and within 72 hours at the latest.

Governance. Security is overseen by the Chief Information Security Officer, who reports to the CEO and provides quarterly updates to the board risk committee. Policies are reviewed at least annually or after material changes to the business or threat environment.

NimbusSec's use of artificial intelligence is governed by an AI policy approved by the executive team and aligned to the Australian Government's AI Ethics Principles and ISO/IEC 42001 concepts. An internal AI review board comprising engineering, legal, and security leadership meets monthly to approve new AI use cases and review incidents. Customers can disable AI-assisted features at the workspace level.

Customer content is never used to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve foundation models, whether our own or third parties'. The platform provides a documented REST API, webhooks, and a native integration marketplace. SCIM 2.0 is supported for automated user provisioning from your identity provider, and SAML 2.0 / OIDC for single sign-on. Custom integrations can be built against the API using scoped, rotatable API keys; rate limits and audit logging apply to all API traffic.

All customer data stored by the platform is encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM. Storage-level encryption is applied across our primary databases, object storage, search indexes, and backups. Encryption keys are managed in AWS KMS with automatic annual key rotation, and key usage is logged to an immutable audit trail. Customer data in our multi-tenant databases is additionally protected by envelope encryption with per-tenant data keys, so that no single key compromise exposes more than one tenant's records. Field-level encryption is applied to particularly sensitive attributes such as API credentials supplied by customers.

NimbusSec engages the following subprocessors to operate the platform: Amazon Web Services (cloud hosting, Sydney and Melbourne regions), OpenAI (LLM inference for document drafting features, with zero data retention agreements in place), Datadog (infrastructure telemetry, metadata only), and Stripe (billing, no access to platform content). Each subprocessor is bound by a data processing agreement with obligations no less protective than our customer commitments. Customers are notified of new subprocessors at least 30 days before onboarding and may object on reasonable grounds. The current register is maintained on our trust portal.

All new personnel complete a structured onboarding program during their first week. Email notifications are sent over opportunistic TLS. Certificates are issued and rotated automatically with a maximum validity of 90 days.
